newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-VICENZA ON TOP OF SERIE A AS MILAN DERBY FINISHES 1-1.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-VICENZA ON TOP OF SERIE A AS MILAN DERBY FINISHES 1-1.

text.p: Vicenza took advantage of Internazionale's 1-1 draw in the Milan derby on Sunday to go clear at the top of the Italian first division for the first time in their 94-year history.
Goals in each half from Gabriele Ambrosetti were enough to see off bottom-of-the-table Reggiana and give Vicenza their first taste of life at the summit of serie A.
Despite briefly sharing the serie A top spot in 1963, the Veneto side has never enjoyed an outright lead in the first division.
Now, with 20 points from 10 matches, unfancied Vicenza lie one ahead of Inter and Bologna, 3-1 winners over Atalanta.
"The title is beyond our ambitions," said manager Francesco Guidolin, "but we're going to enjoy this moment of history."
Inter, who led the table at the start of the day, made the worst possible start to a tenacious derby with AC Milan, falling behind to a Roberto Baggio goal in just four minutes.
Frenchman Marcel Desailly put the former European footballer of the year through to delicately lift the ball over the advancing Gianluca Pagliuca and into the back of the net.
Within eight minutes Inter were level. Paolo Maldini was judged to have pulled down Ivan Zamorano in the area and French playmaker Youri Djorkaeff converted the spot kick.
Despite dominating the second half , Milan failed to secure the win they badly needed to close the gap on their arch-rivals.
Croat Zvonimir Boban came closest, rounding Pagliuca in the 36th minute, only to see his shot cleared off the line by Massimo Paganin.
The dropped points keep the champions five points behindVicenza with three other teams, Sampdoria, Roma and Perugia, on 15 points.
Bologna, who won their last league title in 1964, made light work of Atalanta once Davide Fortunato deflected Cristiano Scapolo's cross past his own goalkeeper in the 22nd minute.
In the 55th minute a first-time shot from Russian Igor Kolyvanov, lurking on the edge of the area, made it 2-0. Pierpaolo Bresciani added a third three minutes later.

Bologna could even afford the luxury of Scapolo's missed penalty in the 65th minute before Atalanta's Felippo Inzaghi joined Abel Balbo as joint top scorer in serie A with his eighth goal of the season.

European champions Juventus, who are in Tokyo for next week's Intercontinental Cup against Argentina's River Plate, lie equal fourth on 16 points with Napoli, who needed a last-minute goal from Fabio Pecchia to draw 1-1 at Cagliari.
Sampdoria were left to rue the 80th minute dismissal of defender Emanuele Pesaresi for a second yellow card in their 1-1 draw with Lazio at the Olympic stadium.
Within a minute of Pesaresi's dismissal the unmarked Paolo Negro equalised Roberto Mancini's fifth minute, a well-judged header.

Roma's scoreless draw at struggling Parma was noteworthy only for the debut of the visitors' Daniele Conti, the 17-year-old son of Bruno Conti who was a key member of Italy's 1982 World Cup winning side.
